title: Spinor Structure from Relativistic Mass-Shell Factorisation in Phase Space
abstract: Spin is usually regarded as one of the most intrinsically quantum phenomena, while its lack of a natural analogue in classical physics presents an obstacle to phase-space deformation-quantisation accounts of its origin. We show that this difficulty may arise from imposing an overly restrictive scalar Hamiltonian structure on relativistic phase space. Requiring the complete massive mass-shell constraint to be represented by a single finite-dimensional expression that is linear in all four components of momentum forces its coefficient matrices to satisfy a Clifford algebra. The minimal complex representation of this algebra is four-dimensional. Requiring statistical completeness within the rank-two subspace selected by the mass-shell factor then leads to a four-by-four matrix-valued ensemble distribution. At each on-shell momentum, the linear mass-shell operator selects a two-dimensional subspace, so a general classical ensemble is described by a $2 \times 2$ matrix before quantisation. Projecting the Weyl-ordered Liouville equation into this subspace gives relativistic transport while preserving arbitrary populations and coherences and the remaining projector components determine the first deformation correction. Expansion of the matrix Moyal star commutator yields the symmetrised classical matrix Liouvillian at leading order. If the stronger two-sided star constraints are imposed, they reproduce the left and right Dirac-Wigner equations and introduce $\hbar$ as the scale converting the dimensionless internal algebra into physical angular momentum. These results suggest a non-quantum origin for spinor structure and a route to reconciling relativistic covariance, classical phase-space transport, and quantum spin.
summary: This paper develops a covariant phase-space framework to investigate the origin of quantum spin in relativistic physics. By analyzing the constraints imposed by the relativistic mass-shell condition on the phase-space dynamics, the authors show that the underlying structure must obey a Clifford algebra. This formalism successfully derives the Dirac-Wigner equations, suggesting that spin structure can arise naturally from relativistic kinematics rather than being an imposed quantum postulate.
main_problem: The paper investigates whether the intrinsic spinor structure of spin-1/2 particles in relativistic quantum mechanics can emerge naturally from the compatibility between relativistic kinematics (mass-shell constraints) and covariant statistical phase-space dynamics.
main_result: The requirement of a linear, covariant mass-shell factor forces the underlying algebraic structure to be a Clifford algebra, suggesting a non-quantum origin for spinor structure and providing a phase-space route to the Dirac-Wigner equations.
method: The authors employ covariant phase-space quantization techniques, projecting the Liouville equation onto the mass-shell subspace and utilizing the Moyal star product expansion to derive classical and quantum transport equations.
model_or_system: The model is relativistic quantum mechanics for spin-1/2 particles, described using a covariant classical phase-space distribution function $W$ constrained by the mass-shell condition $p_\mu p^\mu = m^2c^2$. The dynamics are governed by the Liouville equation.

important_parameters: The reduced Planck constant ($\hbar$) acts as the scale converting the dimensionless internal algebra into physical angular momentum, while the mass $m$ sets the scale for the mass-shell constraint.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the statistical description must be covariant and that the mass-shell constraint can be factorized linearly in momentum components.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the problem by noting the difficulty of deriving spin classically. It then imposes the mass-shell constraint, forcing the coefficient matrices into a Clifford algebra. The dynamics are analyzed by projecting the Liouville equation into the resulting $2 	imes 2$ subspace, leading to the symmetric Liouvillian and ultimately reproducing the Dirac-Wigner equations via the Moyal star commutator.
why_interesting: This work provides a deep theoretical link between fundamental symmetries (Lorentz covariance, mass-shell constraints) and quantum properties (spin), offering a non-standard, phase-space approach to quantum foundations that is relevant to advanced quantum field theory.
